purpose: Measure the existing full Flash-Next serving path under cold and shared-prefix agent traffic before selecting a pruning or prefiller implementation.

hardware_and_model.gpus: 2 x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti, split 30 with the CPU-root card first

workload.prompt_source: 40,000 bytes selected from real Strata C++/CUDA source (13,950-13,975 prompt tokens depending on the agent suffix)

arms.unique_cold: 4 requests per round, each with a unique nonce before the shared code document; all prompt tokens are read fresh
arms.shared_prefix: one priming request followed by 3 requests per round using strata_prefix on message 1; the priming request is cold and the next 3 reuse the common prefix

routing_trace.scope: serve verify-window routing records; unit weights, therefore routed-activation coverage only

subagent_audits.result: identified engine DONE/stderr metrics, /metrics, serve_load/research_run, and routing-trace seams; warned that serve traces are activation-only and instrumentation can perturb timing
found the current Coder revision/allocation change and required profile remapping through original expert indices
recommended a 256-expert existing UD-IQ4_XS-style first custom decoder, BF16 heal before quantization, and dense-before-hot-expert prefiller staging
pinned current Coder and 27B template revisions, exact file sizes/hashes, and distinguished paper measurements from released-runtime behavior

interpretation.prefix_reuse: For this workload, a held 13,943-token prefix reduced the median fresh-prompt read from 4,159.5 ms to 192 ms, about 21.7x less fresh-read time. This is prompt-cache reuse, not model speedup.
interpretation.current_bottleneck: With 99.9211% aggregate decode expert-cache hits, this warm full-model workload is not decode-expert-miss bound. Pruning may still improve footprint, startup, cold-agent behavior, concurrency headroom, and cache resilience, but those must be measured.
interpretation.routing_ladder: A 64-experts-per-layer hot set covers 92.0833% of routed activations in this decode trace; 96 covers 98.2667% and 128 covers 99.6833%. These are in-sample activation shares, not quality retention or prompt-prefill coverage.

validation.command: remote B550 HTTP sweep against the resident Strata server
validation.result: 24/24 requests completed across 3 cold and 3 shared-prefix rounds
1,200 records, exactly 25 per layer and all 48 layers present
10 focused planner tests passed after mode-specific coverage semantics were added
completed after this full-model baseline; see evidence/coder-current-runtime-stats-2026-10-20.json

non_claims: The Coder control was a separate current-revision scratch artifact, not the setup.py-pinned installer family.
The workload is real source text but not a full production agent transcript with tool calls.
Client concurrency is four, while this server configuration serializes requests through a FIFO; no batch-slot throughput claim is made.
The routing trace does not capture batched prompt-prefill routing and cannot select a complete prefiller mask by itself.
Activation coverage does not imply KL, benchmark, or answer quality retention.
The server used split-30 two-GPU execution; the all-layer trace used a separate single-GPU run and was slower, so its timing is not part of the sweep comparison.
No cold KV tier was enabled in this runtime-statistics arm.
